correctness.rationale: Example 5.3 gives the displayed three summands; their weight differences contain a unimodular basis and fix the full character lattice. Independent replay (python3 /workspace/replay/crown_polyhedra.py, standard library) checks the eight proposed supporting inequalities: all 22 sums satisfy them, and the bounded intersection has ten vertices, all among the sums, so the descriptions agree. Eight maximal cones have three unimodular rays. The remaining two have the displayed independent four-ray circuits with two positive and two negative coefficients of unit absolute value; each triple is unimodular. In each case a basis identifies the cone with the height-one conifold cone on e1,e2,e3,−e1+e2+e3. Its dual monoid consists of nonnegative triples with A≤B+C, generated by the four stated elements with one binomial relation, giving an isolated node. Any equivariant resolution is an isomorphism on the dense torus and hence a fan refinement, and smallness allows no new rays. Only the two choices of diagonal per node are available. Exact triple-plane checks on the four rational support perturbations yield 12 unimodular maximal cones in each, all refining the old fan and retaining precisely its rays, with all four distinct diagonal pairs. These are normal fans of bounded rational polytopes, so the resolving varieties and the maps to the separated X are projective. Refinements cannot be identified over X by permuting rays, since an isomorphism over X is the identity on the dense torus. Locally a rank-one 2-by-2 matrix with a chosen column line gives an exceptional zero section in the direct sum of two tautological lines on P¹; choosing a row line gives the other small resolution, related by the Atiyah flop. The two node neighborhoods give disjoint exceptional curves, and the Cartier canonical divisor has no discrepancy terms for a small morphism. The smooth projective toric divisor/cohomology calculation gives rho=b2=8−3=5, b4=5 by duality, and only b0=b6=1 beyond these. No non-toric classification is inferred.

value.rationale: The 4-crown is a concrete nonsmooth Richardson example singled out by the initiating toricity work. Knowing both local conifold choices does not in general tell whether either combination is globally projective. This gives the full projective model and single-curve flop graph over that naturally specified target, with invariants useful for comparing the models; there is no extrapolation to arbitrary Richardson varieties.
